IX.5 p136v.text: But we need not say more upon this Point, and if what we have here laid down appears to be true, we may conclude Beauty to be such a Consent and Agreement of the Parts of a Whole in which it is found, as to Number, Finishing and Collocation, as Congruity, that is to say, the principal Law of Nature requires. This is what Architecture chiefly aims at, and by this she obtains her Beauty, Dignity and Value.
IX.5 p136v.verification: maker compared scan; independent reader, rights, completeness and alignment with Latin pending

research_update: A separate research reader checked 1541 fol. 136v and 1755 p. 195 on 19 November. The two English sentences correspond to three Latin sentences; absoluta primariaque ratio naturae is shortened to principal Law of Nature, and the last Latin sequence is rendered more freely. John Ozell is credited as English translator of the 1726 edition by the Met; Leoni is named on the 1755 title. Their precise contributions to this passage need further evidence. Bartoli mediates the translation, and the Italian passage has not yet been independently checked. Latin scan reads autoritatem where accepted packet has auctoritatem; owner notified separately. No formal kit review.
